result.title: Automated Call for Action: RAG-Based Environmental Law Enforcement Screening System
result.summary: Environmental law inspectors face a structural issue in identifying potential violations from data: they often do not have the capacity to deal with large volume of data present in the emission events. This paper examines to what extent an LLM-based system can support evidence assembly and permit-based screening of such events, using the coke plants of a steel producer and a regional environmental service as a case. A simple puff-trajectory model aligns air quality measurements, weather and citizen complaints with each emission event. A retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) pipeline then retrieves facility-specific permit conditions and generates event reports and a period report with an investigation recommendation. Across 74 events from March 2025, plant-aware re-ranking reduced reports citing the other plant's conditions from 58.1% (hybrid retrieval) to 0% by rule-based plant labels, while maintaining high RAGAS and LLM-judge metrics. GPT-5-mini performed comparably to GPT-5.1, whereas GPT-5-nano scored lower on legal grounding and legal faithfulness. In an evidence ablation, removing air quality (AQ) data changed judge scores and period recommendations most; citation overlap changed only slightly under any removal, and removing complaint details had no measurable effect. This suggests a need for rules and guidelines that link complaints to incidents and permit conditions, so that community reports can count as evidence. The results support screening of events that may need further investigation. Design implications for involving environmental service experts are derived.

AI.brief_summary: 论文构建面向环境执法的 LLM/RAG 筛查系统：用烟羽轨迹模型把空气质量、气象与居民投诉对齐到排放事件，再检索设施许可条件生成事件与周期报告及调查建议，并以 plant-aware 重排和证据消融评估报告质量。
AI.relevance_reason: 其按证据来源逐一消融、并用引用重叠与 LLM 评审判定证据是否真被使用，可能可供核查 LVR 中视觉证据筛选与「视觉旁路、贡献分配」的诊断式评测设计；但该任务本身与视觉及 latent 推理状态无直接联系。
